newsitem.title: USA: FoxMeyer to sell unit to McKesson.
newsitem.headline: FoxMeyer to sell unit to McKesson.

text.p: FoxMeyer Health Corp. will sell its bankrupt drug distribution unit, FoxMeyer Drug Co., and certain affiliates to rival McKesson Corp. for about $80 million in cash, the companies said Friday.
McKesson, with annual revenues of $14 billion, is the largest pharmaceutical and health care products distributor in North America.

FoxMeyer Drug -- the nation's fourth-largest wholesaler of pharmaceutical products, health and beauty aids -- filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection Aug. 27. It has about 2,200 employees in 21 states and Washington.
The sale marks FoxMeyer Health's exit from the health care distribution business, which the Dallas-based company has treated as a discontinued operation since its June 30 quarterly financial report.
The value of the deal is subject to FoxMeyer meeting certain financial targets and how much money the company collects from vendors that have yet to pay for previously delivered goods.
McKesson will provide $30 million to FoxMeyer by participating in FoxMeyer's debtor-in-possession financing, which allows the company to borrow 70 cents for every $1 of inventory held.
These funds will enable FoxMeyer to buy about $100 million of additional inventory and help to revive its business.

After the deal closes, McKesson will discharge FoxMeyer's obligations under the debtor-in-possession financing with G.E. Capital Corp., and assume substantially all other liabilities of the company, FoxMeyer said.
Proceeds from the sale will be used to discharge FoxMeyer's liabilities and pay off creditors.

Separately, San Francisco-based McKesson said the acquisition would boost earnings within 90 to 180 days after the deal closes in mid-November, subject to approval by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware and regulators.
FoxMeyer's stock was unchanged at $3.50, while McKesson rose $2.875 to $48.325 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon.
